subject: Follow-up: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Hi Beth 

Thanks for the call today  really helpful to hear more about EdgeFin's latency and streaming needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Recap
- Primary SLOs you mentioned: p95 latency target for streaming generation; acceptable tail behavior for concurrent sessions.
- Expected concurrency: ~50 simultaneous sessions during peak, with bursts to ~150 for short windows.
- Throughput: steady-state ~200 req/s, burst to ~600 req/s.
- Streaming: client needs partial-token streaming (time-to-first-token important) and per-token steady throughput.

Proposed next steps
1) Share our benchmark methodology and the prompt set we used as a first pass (attached).
2) Confirm exact measurement definitions (time-to-first-token vs end-to-end last-token) and environment for reproducibility.
3) Schedule an engineering benchmark run with your team present (we can run in our Dedicated env or send harness for you to run).
4) Agree on pass/fail thresholds for the evaluation (we should both sign off on the SLA targets to avoid surprises).

For transparency, attached is a first-pass prompt_set_edgefin.csv and our benchmark_harness_v1.zip (harness + README). Key notes in the doc: we measure both cold-start and warm (warm = after 10 warm-up requests), we capture time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-to-last-token (TTLT), and we isolate network latency by using a colocated load generator where possible.

Can you confirm the p95 and concurrency numbers above, and let me know if you prefer us to run the first benchmark or if you'll run it on your side? Once you confirm, Rafael and Neha (cc'd) will coordinate the config and scheduling.

Thanks 
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments: prompt_set_edgefin.csv (csv), benchmark_harness_v1.zip (zip)

From: Beth Carter <beth.carter@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Hi Marissa 

Thanks for the recap  this looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SLOs: target p95 <= 250ms for time-to-first-token and p95 <= 900ms for time-to-last-token on our typical 512-token prompts. The team is comfortable with higher tail for very long responses (>1024 tokens) but want clear visibility.
- Concurrency: 50 steady concurrent sessions is accurate; we need to verify how the system behaves at 150 concurrent sessions during 2 5 minute spikes.
- Throughput: steady 200 req/s, burst up to 600 req/s for short windows.
- Streaming: yes  we need partial-token streaming; time-to-first-token is critical for perceived responsiveness. We use SSE-based streaming in our client.

We'd like to see your harness measure TTFT and TTLT separately, and also provide per-client observed stats (so we can correlate with our frontend measurements). If you can include the exact harness config and a reproducible prompt set that'd be great.

We'd prefer Redwood to run the first pass in your Dedicated test bed so we can watch and iterate. Please include warm-up procedure and whether batching will be enabled during the test (we prefer an option with batching off to reflect single-request latency and another run with batching on for cost/throughput trade-offs).

Thanks  I'll coordinate internally and confirm a 2-hour window next week for the live run.

Beth
Beth Carter
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeFin
beth.carter@edgefin.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@edgefin.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Hi Beth 

Great  thanks for the clarity. We'll run the first pass in our Dedicated test bed and invite your team to join. Details below: 

Benchmark plan (high-level)
- Runs: 3 phases  cold-start baseline, warm baseline (after 10 warm-ups), and sustained concurrency/throughput sweep including burst windows.
- Measurements: time-to-first-token (TTFT), time-to-last-token (TTLT), per-request token-rate, p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, CPU/GPU utilization, and memory/KV cache hit rate.
- Environment: Dedicated cluster (pinned model version + quantization profile), colocated load generator in same region for network isolation.
- Batching: We'll do both  run A: batching disabled (single-request latency), run B: batching enabled (optimized throughput). We'll include config for both.
- Reproducibility: harness records RNG seeds, model hash, kernel config, and exact prompt set. We'll publish a README with steps to reproduce on your side.

Attachments and links
- prompt_set_edgefin.csv (custom prompt set reflecting your mix of short/long prompts)
- benchmark_harness_v1.zip (harness + runner + minimal README)
- ef_benchmark_config.yaml (bench config with warm-up, concurrency schedule, and metrics capture)  attached.
- Shared doc with measurement definitions: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cEdgeFinBenchDoc

Next steps
1) Rafael / Neha to validate ef_benchmark_config.yaml and confirm whether we should disable continuous batching and set KV cache warm-up to 10 requests (suggested).
2) I'll propose two 2-hour windows for the live run next week once Rafael confirms infra readiness.
3) After runs, we'll share raw harness logs and a reproducible run book.

Rafael / Neha  can you review the attached config and confirm ETA for the Dedicated test bed prep?

Thanks all 
Marissa

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Beth Carter <beth.carter@edgefin.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance SLO qualification & benchmark methodology

Thanks Marissa  quick engineering notes from my side: 

- Config review: ef_benchmark_config.yaml looks good. Agree with 10-request KV warm-up and capturing both TTFT and TTLT.
- Batching: we'll disable continuous batching for the single-request runs (Run A) to reflect realistic p95 client latency. For run B we'll enable batching with a max batch latency of 10ms to approximate production throughput behavior.
- Reproducibility: we'll pin the model hash, record kernel selection, and snapshot the inference runtime config. We'll also capture GPU power/clock and CUDA driver versions in the logs.
- Load pattern: recommend using a poisson arrival for steady-state with 50 concurrent clients and short spike windows (3 minutes) to 150 concurrent clients  we'll simulate both.
- Expected baseline (rough): for a 512-token prompt on our Dedicated n1g.4x (example) we typically see TTFT ~120 180ms (p95 depends on concurrency/batching) and TTLT ~600 800ms for 512 tokens without aggressive quantization. We'll treat these as a reference, not a promise.

I'll schedule infra prep for Thursday and Friday this week. Once prepared we'll run a dry-run and share the raw harness logs to the Drive link and to hubspot record DEAL-2047.

Rafael
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Attachment: ef_benchmark_config.yaml (yaml)
